scores.rationale: None of the snippets directly address the relationship between chlorophyll-to-carbon ratio (chl:C) and dilution rate under nutrient-limiting conditions. The corpus consists largely of off-topic reproduction-focused abstracts (plant cleistogamy/chasmogamy, whale calving, rice fertilizers, rotifer diet quality) that merely mention chlorophyll or nutrients in passing. The only snippet bearing on chlorophyll regulation under nutrient stress is [11], which describes a decrease in cellular Chl content during nitrogen deprivation due to growth-dilution; if anything this runs counter to (or at least does not affirm) the stated fact that chl:C increases with dilution rate under limitation. There is no clear supporting evidence and only weak, tangential opposing evidence, so the corpus is essentially insufficient to evaluate the stylized fact.
